name.text: Shared: Apply rounding in a real-world context

questiontext.text:
A school records the number of exercise books distributed during a term as \[ {@quantity@}. \]

For a short report, the head teacher wants the quantity stated to the nearest {@place_name@}.

What value should be reported?

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

The original quantity is \[ {@quantity@}. \]

The report only requires the nearest {@place_name@}, so the quantity should not be reported with more precision than requested.

The appropriate reported value is \[ \boxed{{@answer@}}. \]

contextual-rounding

Learners apply rounding to a reporting context rather than performing an isolated calculation.

Targets reporting unjustified precision when a context explicitly requests a rounded quantity, with truncation as a secondary misconception.

Original STACK question. No external wording or mathematical content is copied.

None.

Curriculum alignment is maintained outside the question source.

prtincorrect.text: Use the precision requested by the reporting context.

node.description: Checks whether the learner reports the unrounded quantity.

truefeedback.text:
That is the exact count, but the report asks for a rounded value.

Reporting every digit gives more precision than the context requires. Round to the requested place.

It looks like you truncated the quantity.

Use the digit immediately to the right of the reporting place to decide whether to round up or down.

falsefeedback.text: Round the quantity to the place requested in the report.

qtest.description: Correct contextual rounding receives full credit.
Reporting the exact unrounded quantity receives zero credit.
Truncating instead of rounding receives zero credit.
